skill.name: writing-plans
skill.description: Create detailed implementation plans after design is complete, with exact files, small tasks, tests, commands, and execution handoff steps.
skill.summary: Turn completed designs into detailed implementation plans for engineers with limited project context.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline backticks in documentation examples. The skill instructs plan writing and includes example test and git commands, but it does not execute commands or process untrusted input. Manual archive review found only the same SKILL.md file, with no hidden payload evidence.

remediation.issue: Example shell commands may be copied into generated plans without project-specific review.
remediation.suggestion: Add wording that all generated commands must be adapted to the target repository and reviewed before execution.

content.value_statement: Engineering teams often lose time when implementation plans assume hidden context. This skill creates clear task plans with files, tests, commands, and handoff steps.
actual_capabilities: Creates implementation plans after architecture and design decisions are settled.
Breaks work into small tasks with explicit files to create, modify, and test.
Prompts for failing tests, minimal implementation, verification commands, and commits.
Includes expected command results so implementers can verify each step.
Defines a handoff choice between subagent-driven execution and a separate execution session.
limitations: It does not choose the architecture or resolve incomplete product requirements.
It assumes the assistant can inspect the target repository for accurate file paths.
Example commands must be adapted before use in repositories with different tooling.
It writes plans only; implementation requires a separate execution workflow.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature build plan
use_cases.description: Convert an approved design into ordered tasks with exact files, tests, and verification steps.

use_cases.title: Hand off work to a new contributor
use_cases.description: Create a plan that assumes little project context and explains the expected implementation path.

use_cases.title: Structure AI-assisted implementation
use_cases.description: Define task boundaries and review checkpoints before using Claude Code or Codex to implement changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic plan
prompt_templates.scenario: A design is complete and needs an implementation plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill to create an implementation plan for this approved design: [paste design]. Include exact files, tests, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan for a new contributor
prompt_templates.scenario: The implementer has little project context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill. Write the plan for an engineer who is new to this codebase. Explain each task with files, commands, expected results, and commits.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a test-driven change
prompt_templates.scenario: The team wants each task to begin with a failing test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill to create a TDD plan for [feature]. Each task must start with a failing test, then minimal code, verification, and a commit.

prompt_templates.title: Plan execution handoff
prompt_templates.scenario: The plan will be executed by another session or subagents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-plans skill for [feature]. Save the plan under docs/plans and end with execution options for subagent-driven or parallel-session implementation.

output_examples.input: Plan a small feature after the design is approved.
output: A saved plan with a clear goal, architecture summary, and technology notes.
Task sections that list files to create, modify, and test.
Verification steps with commands, expected outcomes, and commit points.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff for an engineer who does not know this repository.
output: A step-by-step plan that avoids assumed project knowledge.
Small tasks that guide test writing, implementation, and validation.
A final choice between same-session subagent execution and a separate execution session.

best_practices: Use this skill only after product requirements and architecture choices are settled.
Inspect the repository first so file paths and commands are accurate.
Keep each task small enough to test and review independently.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to decide architecture when the design is still unclear.
Do not leave placeholders where exact paths, tests, or commands are needed.
Do not execute generated commands without reviewing them for the target repository.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after design is complete and before implementation starts. It turns decisions into concrete engineering tasks.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It writes an implementation plan with examples, tests, commands, and verification steps.

faq.question: Can it help with TDD?
faq.answer: Yes. The task format asks for a failing test before minimal implementation and verification.

faq.question: Why does it ask for exact file paths?
faq.answer: Exact paths reduce ambiguity for engineers and AI agents that have limited codebase context.

faq.question: Is it safe to publish?
faq.answer: The reviewed content is documentation-focused. Example commands should still be reviewed before execution.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
